top_stories.title: Bitcoin Nears $100k Amid Strong ETF Inflows
points: Bitcoin trading near $100,000 as crypto markets show recovery momentum driven by institutional investment and reduced regulatory pressure.
US spot bitcoin ETFs added $528.4M on Wednesday, the largest single day in nearly a month; IBIT contributed $235M and Fidelity FBTC $212.7M (~85% of inflows).
Three-session cumulative inflows exceeded $1B this week; total net inflows near $58B with net assets of $109.3B across all bitcoin ETFs.
Ether ETFs returned to inflows of $14.9M, ending a five-day outflow streak; traders awaiting Fed decision October 28 and US election November 3.
Bitcoin's 28-day realized volatility (a measure of price swings) fell to 1.2%, near this year's low, indicating subdued trading activity.

unique_angles.point: $100k milestone would represent a significant psychological barrier breakthrough for mainstream adoption narratives.

items.title: JPMorgan Brings Tokenized Funds to Solana
points: JPMorgan deployed tokenized funds on Solana, following earlier deployments on other networks, expanding institutional asset offerings beyond Ethereum.
Move signals institutional confidence in Solana's infrastructure for real-world asset tokenization (converting traditional financial assets into blockchain-based digital tokens).
Major financial institutions now treat multiple blockchains as viable platforms rather than betting on a single network.
Solana's lower transaction costs and faster settlement times are seen as competitive advantages for high-volume institutional operations.

items.title: Solana's Alpenglow Upgrade Goes Live
points: Solana activated Alpenglow, cutting transaction finality from several seconds to ~150 milliseconds, its biggest network upgrade since 2020.
Validators now send votes directly to each other and combine approvals into certificates instead of recording votes as transactions.
Blocks can finalize after one or two voting rounds instead of requiring votes across successive blocks; 446 of 654 validators voted on the starting block.
Exchanges can credit deposits sooner and payment processors can confirm stablecoin transactions faster; wallets, fees, and app behavior remain unchanged.
Transaction totals will show a sharp drop on dashboards since validator votes no longer appear as transactions, though actual user activity is unchanged.

items.title: Daily.fun Launches Beta for Consumer Prediction Markets
points: Daily.fun launched beta for consumer prediction markets with card-pack mechanics designed to make onchain trading more accessible.

items.title: Starknet Community Backs Post-Quantum Independence
points: 93.5% voting power across 2,800+ wallets supported moving from Ethereum Layer 2 to an independent post-quantum Layer 1 (a blockchain using hash-based cryptography resistant to quantum computers) in a seven-day Snapshot poll; StarkWare did not vote.
Draft whitepaper expected in November; STRK token holders must vote again on any actual transition, with no guaranteed timeline.
Starknet's hash-based cryptography allows accounts to adopt post-quantum signatures without protocol changes, but security still inherits from the Ethereum bridge until full independence.
As an Ethereum L2, the network is only as quantum-safe as Ethereum itself; full independence would eliminate this dependency.

items.title: XMTP Pivots to Open-Source After Web3 Bet Failed
points: XMTP Labs is shutting down its hosted messaging network in early 2027, transitioning to open-source, self-hosted software after its early Web3 identity and token strategy failed to generate developer demand.

No token will launch; CTO Nick Molnar consolidated the backend into a single Rust binary supporting attachments, push notifications, handles, and signed webhooks with SDKs for mobile, web, servers, and agents.
Developers can run the full stack, inspect code, and set their own policies; self-hosted deployments are isolated by default but agents from different companies can coordinate on the same backend.
Agents no longer require wallet integration, marking a shift from a centralized service to a decentralized infrastructure model.
